newsitem.title: USA: Carter-Wallace's major stockholder rejects Davis offer.
newsitem.headline: Carter-Wallace's major stockholder rejects Davis offer.

text.p: Billionaire investor Marvin Davis said on Friday he was committed to buying Carter-Wallace Inc. for $835 million, but would consider a higher bid "if one can be justified."

Davis responded to a statement earlier Friday in which the maker of Trojan condoms and Arrid deodorant said its majority shareholder, CPI Development Corp., had no interest in a deal at Davis' $18 a share bid.
The stock fell 87.50 cents to $14.625 in New York Stock Exchange trading.
"We reiterate our commitment to negotiate to acquire the company for $18 a share," Davis said in a letter addressed to the Carter-Wallace board and made public by Davis.
"Moreover, as we have previously indicated, we would be willing to offer a higher price if one can be justified," Davis added.
Carter-Wallace had said that in light of CPI Development's position, it will not take any further action on Davis' bid.
Davis said he thought the Carter-Wallace board had ceded its fiduciary responsibility to CPI by letting it "dictate" the company's position on the bid.
"Given the company's lackluster performance, we believe that the board has an enhanced obligation to review all alternatives before rejecting an offer," Davis said.

Most traders had given the buyout deal only a slim chance of succeeding because Carter-Wallace has previously expressed little interest in selling the company. Furthermore, insiders control about 82 percent of Carter-Wallace via common stock and a special class of shares.

Carter-Wallace is dominated by members of the Hoyt family. Chief Executive Officer and Chairman Henry Hoyt Jr. is the son of the executive who took over management of the Carter Medicine Company in 1929. Family members hold other key positions.

Carter-Wallace has long been viewed on Wall Street as an acquisition candidate. At the company's meeting in July, some stockholders criticised its low stock price but a shareholder proposal to consider a merger was rejected.
